title: VI–XIII. Degrees and modes: public preaching, singular revelation, direct and indirect
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Ye degrees belonging toward heavenly calling stand as those according toward which it stands as either belonging toward public preaching or belonging toward singular revelation. — VI. — Ye ordinary stands as that which ye Holy Spirit used under ye Old Testament in responses from ye mercy-seat and through Urim and Thummim. — IX. — Singular revelation stands as ordinary or extraordinary. — VIII. — 1:28). — Col. — Acts 17:30; — 28:19; — That belonging toward public preaching stands as that by which ye grace belonging toward redemption stands as announced toward ye whole world and seriously offered (Matt. — VII. — abundant calling stands as that which stands as efficaciously applied toward ye elect. — Sufficient calling stands as that which stands as seriously proposed toward all humans; — Indirect stands as that by which ye Holy Spirit leads humans toward Christ through secondary means. — XIII. — It stands as direct or indirect. — XI.
pass_b_english: VI. The degrees of heavenly calling are those according to which it is either of public preaching or of singular revelation.

VII. That of public preaching is that by which the grace of redemption is announced to the whole world and seriously offered (Matt. 28:19; Acts 17:30; Col. 1:28). VIII. Singular revelation is ordinary or extraordinary. IX. The ordinary is that which the Holy Spirit used under the Old Testament in responses from the mercy-seat and through Urim and Thummim.

XI. It is direct or indirect. XIII. Indirect is that by which the Holy Spirit leads humans to Christ through secondary means. Sufficient calling is that which is seriously proposed to all humans; abundant calling is that which is efficaciously applied to the elect.
source_text: VI. Gradus supernae vocationis sunt, secundum quos 1. est publicae praedicationis aut singularis revelationis. VII. Publicae praedicationis est, qua gratia redemtionis toti mundo annunciatur & serio offertur, Matth. 28:19; Act. 17:30; Col. 1:28. VIII. Singularis revelationis est ordinaria aut extraordinaria. IX. Ordinaria est, qua Spiritus sanctus usus est sub V.T. in responsis ex propitiatorio & per Urim & Thummim. XI. Est directa aut indirecta. XIII. Indirecta est, qua Spiritus sanctus per media secundaria homines ad Christum ducit. Sufficiens vocatio est quae omnibus hominibus serio proponitur; abundans quae electis efficaciter applicatur.
